display.title: Episode 194: The Sly Fox and the Cheese (Erev Yom Kippur)
display.summary_short: An Erev Yom Kippur show: candle lighting, the Alter Rebbe's Avinu Malkeinu tune, and the fable of the fox in the well, a lesson in outsmarting the yetzer hara.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Erev Yom Kippur 5746, just before candle lighting. Uncle Yossi gives the candle time and brachos, explains that on Yom Kippur we turn to Hashem as both our Father and our King, and plays the Alter Rebbe's tune for Avinu Malkeinu. After an announcement of the Tzivos Hashem Sukkos Experience, he tells the fable 'The Hungry Fox and the Barrel of Cheese': a starving fox mistakes the moon's reflection in a well for cheese, lowers himself in a bucket and finds only water, with no way back up. A Beis Rivkah third-grader leads the Shema. Uncle Yossi then teaches that the Torah was given to people, not angels, because we have a yetzer hara that tries to trick us, and that a soldier of Hashem should not argue with it but ignore it. The fable ends as the fox sings happily until a second fox, fooled into thinking there is cheese below, rides down and lifts him out. The yetzer hara is just as sly; our three secret weapons are Torah, davening and tzedakah. The show closes with a note that it will be off for Sukkos and Simchas Torah and back on 15 October.
display.lesson: The yetzer hara is tricky, so don't argue with it; ignore it, and fight it with Torah, davening and tzedakah.

date.note: 'Today is Erev Yom Kippur'; candle lighting 6:32 in New York; 'back on the air the 15th of October'.
